newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast late spot prods flat as trade idles.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast late spot prods flat as trade idles.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot unleaded gasoline prices were unchanged Thursday amidst limited activity and a lack of concern about supplies, traders said.
Distillate prices, which have fallen nearly 10 percent since the mid-April, also held at Wednesday's levels.
Trade was sapped because many West Coast traders left the market to attend a popular industry function in Texas.
Traders said gasoline would stay under pressure given last week's 1.4-million-barrel build in West Coast gasoline stocks, which put supplies at 28.1 million barrels
CARB diesel in Los Angeles remained 63/64 cents a gallon Thursday, after falling eight cents the last week.

Distillate stocks, including diesel, stood at 11.5 million barrels, nearly the same as last week's levels which saw a year-on-year increase of 1.1 million barrels, according to the American Petroleum Institute (API).
CARB unleaded gasoline stood 67/68 cents, also flat from Wednesday, while conventional grades, for sale outside California, were steady at 63.50/64.50 cents.
